title: Choosing a Research Question That Matters (FINER)

hook.en: Most student projects fail before the first patient is recruited, because the question was too big, too vague or impossible to answer with the time and people available. A good question is half the research. FINER is a quick test to find out whether yours is one.
hook.ur: Zyada tar talba ke projects pehle mareez ke bharti hone se pehle hi nakam ho jate hain, kyunke sawal bohat bara, bohat mubham ya dastiyab waqt aur logon se jawab dene ke na-qabil tha. Achha sawal aadhi research hai. FINER ek tez test hai jo batata hai ke aap ka sawal achha hai ya nahi.

goal.en: By the end, you'll turn a topic into a focused question, test it against the FINER criteria (Feasible, Interesting, Novel, Ethical, Relevant), write aims and a hypothesis, and decide whether to narrow or drop an idea.
goal.ur: End tak aap mauzu ko markooz sawal mein badlenge, FINER ke criteria (Feasible, Interesting, Novel, Ethical, Relevant) se test karenge, maqasid aur hypothesis likhenge, aur tay karenge ke khayal ko tang karein ya chhor dein.

text.en: A **topic** ("back pain") is not a **question**. Move from topic to **problem** (what is unknown or unsettled?) to a **research question** (a focused, answerable query with patients, an intervention or exposure, a comparison and an outcome). Then test it with **FINER**: **F**easible (enough patients, time, skills and money), **I**nteresting (to you and to others), **N**ovel (adds something new or confirms something in a new setting), **E**thical (can be done safely and fairly) and **R**elevant (matters to patients, clinicians or policy). A **hypothesis** is a testable prediction; **aims** state what you will do.
text.ur: **Mauzu** ("peeth dard") **sawal** nahi. Mauzu se **masla** (kya na-maloom ya ghair-tay shuda hai?) aur phir **research sawal** (markooz, jawab dene ke qabil sawal jis mein mareez, intervention ya exposure, muqabla aur nateeja ho) tak jayein. Phir **FINER** se test karein: **F**easible (kaafi mareez, waqt, maharat aur paisa), **I**nteresting (aap aur doosron ke liye), **N**ovel (kuch naya jorta ya naye halaat mein tasdeeq karta), **E**thical (mehfooz aur munsifana tareeqe se ho sakta) aur **R**elevant (mareezon, clinicians ya policy ke liye ahem). **Hypothesis** aazmaye ja sakne wali peshgoi hai; **aims** batate hain aap kya karenge.

text.en: Think of **choosing a destination before a trip**. "I want to travel" is a topic. "I want to reach Hunza in August with a budget of 50,000 rupees" is a question you can plan for. FINER is the checklist: can I afford it, is it interesting, has anyone gone this route before, is it safe, and is it worth going?
text.ur: **Safar se pehle manzil chunna** sochein. "Mujhe safar karna hai" mauzu hai. "Mujhe August mein 50,000 rupay ke budget mein Hunza pohanchna hai" aisa sawal hai jis ka plan ban sakta hai. FINER checklist hai: kya main afford kar sakta hoon, dilchasp hai, kya kisi ne yeh raasta liya, mehfooz hai, aur jaane ke qabil hai?

steps.title: Start with a real problem
steps.detail: Write something you noticed in practice: "Many of my patients stop their home exercises after two weeks." || Asal masle se shuru karein

steps.title: Check what is already known
steps.detail: Do a quick search (see the lesson on finding evidence). If a good review answers it, choose a different question. || Dekhein pehle se kya maloom hai

steps.title: Narrow it with PICO
steps.detail: For example: "In adults after knee replacement, does a weekly phone call, compared with usual care, improve exercise completion at 12 weeks?" || PICO se tang karein

steps.title: Run the FINER test
steps.detail: Ask each letter honestly, and write what you would change if the answer is "no". || FINER test chalayein

steps.title: Write one aim and one hypothesis
steps.detail: "Aim: to test whether weekly phone calls increase exercise completion. Hypothesis: completion will be at least 15 percentage points higher with calls." || Ek aim aur ek hypothesis likhein

question.en: A student wants to study "the effect of physiotherapy on all musculoskeletal pain in Pakistan". Which FINER letter is most obviously a problem?
question.ur: Ek talib-e-ilm "Pakistan mein tamam musculoskeletal dard par physiotherapy ka asar" study karna chahta hai. FINER ka kaun sa harf sab se wazeh masla hai?

text.en: Novel, because nobody has studied musculoskeletal pain
text.ur: Novel, kyunke kisi ne musculoskeletal dard study nahi kiya

feedback.ur: Bohat kuch study ho chuka hai.

text.en: Feasible: the question is far too broad for any single study to answer
text.ur: Feasible: sawal bohat wasi hai ke koi ek study jawab de sake

feedback.en: Yes — it needs narrowing to one condition, one intervention and one outcome.
feedback.ur: Haan — isay ek halat, ek intervention aur ek nateeje tak tang karna hoga.

question.en: A therapist finds three recent systematic reviews that already answer her question clearly. Which FINER criterion is weak?
question.ur: Ek therapist ko teen haal ke systematic reviews milte hain jo uska sawal pehle se saaf jawab dete hain. FINER ka kaun sa criterion kamzor hai?

feedback.en: The question may still be relevant.
feedback.ur: Sawal phir bhi relevant ho sakta hai.

text.en: Novel: it adds little new, so she should change the question or look at a gap
text.ur: Novel: yeh kam naya jorta hai, isliye sawal badlein ya kisi kami par dekhein

feedback.en: Yes — a gap is better than a repeat.
feedback.ur: Haan — kami dohrane se behtar hai.

question.en: Which of these is a testable hypothesis?
question.ur: In mein se aazmaye ja sakne wali hypothesis kaun si hai?

text.en: Patients who receive weekly calls will complete at least 15 percentage points more of their prescribed sessions than those who do not
text.ur: Haftawar call walon ne tajweez shuda sessions ka kam az kam 15 fisad points zyada mukammal kiya hoga na ke walon se

feedback.ur: Haan — khaas, naapne ke qabil aur ghalat sabit ho sakne wali.

text.ur: Physiotherapy mareezon ke liye achhi hai

text.en: **Falling in love with a topic or a method.** "I want to use a new device" is not a question. And a question that would change nothing whatever the result is not worth asking. Test the "so what?" by asking: if the result is positive, what will I do differently; if negative, what will I do? If you cannot answer, rethink.
text.ur: **Mauzu ya tareeqe se ishq ho jana.** "Mujhe naya aala istemal karna hai" sawal nahi. Aur woh sawal jo nateeje se koi farq na daale poochne ke qabil nahi. "Phir kya?" ka test poochhein: agar nateeja musbat ho to main kya mukhtalif karunga; agar manfi ho to kya karunga? Jawab na ho to dobara sochein.

text.en: **Ask your patients and colleagues.** The best questions come from the clinic floor: "What worries you most about recovery?", "What do you wish we knew?" Patients can suggest questions you would never think of, and research that matters to them is more likely to be useful. Keep a notebook of puzzles you meet each week.
text.ur: **Apne mareezon aur saathiyon se poochhein.** Behtareen sawal clinic ki zameen se aate hain: "Recovery ke baare mein sab se zyada kya fikr hai?", "Kaash hum kya jaante?" Mareez aise sawal suggest kar sakte hain jo aap kabhi nahi sochte, aur woh research jo un ke liye ahem ho mufeed hone ka zyada imkaan rakhti hai. Har haftay jin pahelion se milte hain unki copy rakhein.

question.en: Is a small, humble question better than a big, bold one?
question.ur: Kya chhota, saada sawal bare, jasoorana sawal se behtar hai?

answer.en: For a student or early researcher, usually yes. A focused question you can answer well beats an ambitious one you cannot complete. Many careers began with a small audit or a case report. Aim to do one thing properly, publish it, and build from there. Bold ideas can grow from small, solid foundations.
answer.ur: Talib-e-ilm ya shuruaati muhaqqiq ke liye aam taur par haan. Markooz sawal jis ka aap achha jawab de sakein bare, jasoorana sawal se behtar hai jo aap mukammal na kar sakein. Bohat se career chhote audit ya case report se shuru hue. Ek kaam theek se karna, shaya karna aur wahin se banana maqsad rakhein. Bare khayalat chhoti, mazboot bunyadon se barh sakte hain.

beats.patient: A physiotherapist notices that stroke patients in her ward often have a painful shoulder. She wonders "how to treat shoulder pain after stroke". The topic is broad.
beats.assessment: Narrowing with PICO and FINER: patients, intervention, comparison and outcome are unclear, and existing reviews cover many treatments.
beats.treatment: She refines to: "In adults within 3 months of stroke with shoulder pain, does teaching carers safe positioning and handling, compared with usual care, reduce pain at 6 weeks?"
beats.reassess: It is feasible in her ward, relevant to patients and carers, novel in her setting, and ethical; she plans a pilot.

text.en: **Check ethics early.** If your question involves vulnerable patients, withholding care or personal data, talk to your ethics committee before building the study. A question that cannot be answered safely should be changed. Also check conflicts of interest, such as a device company funding the question.
text.ur: **Ethics jaldi dekhein.** Agar aap ke sawal mein kamzor mareez, care rokna ya zaati data shamil ho to study banane se pehle ethics committee se baat karein. Jo sawal mehfooz tareeqe se jawab na pa sakay usay badlein. Mufaadat ke takrao bhi dekhein, jaise aala banane wali company ka sawal ko funding dena.

text.en: Hulley and colleagues introduced the FINER criteria in their standard text on clinical research design as a way to judge whether a research question is Feasible, Interesting, Novel, Ethical and Relevant. Farrugia and colleagues described how good research questions arise from a clear problem, are focused and answerable, and lead to well-defined hypotheses and objectives, and that vague or overly broad questions are a common reason studies fail.
text.ur: Hulley aur saathiyon ne clinical research design ki apni mayaari kitab mein FINER criteria pesh kiye taake parkha ja sake ke research sawal Feasible, Interesting, Novel, Ethical aur Relevant hai ya nahi. Farrugia aur saathiyon ne bayan kiya ke achhe research sawal saaf masle se nikalte hain, markooz aur jawab dene ke qabil hote hain, aur saaf hypotheses aur maqasid tak le jate hain, aur ke mubham ya bohat wasi sawal studies ke nakam hone ki aam wajah hain.

text.en: **Problem, PICO, FINER, So what?** Start with a problem, shape it with PICO, test with FINER and ask "so what?"
text.ur: **Masla, PICO, FINER, Phir kya?** Masle se shuru, PICO se shakal, FINER se test aur "phir kya?" poochhein.

summary.en: Move from topic to problem to a focused PICO-style question, then test it with FINER.
summary.ur: Mauzu se masla aur phir markooz PICO-style sawal tak jayein, phir FINER se test karein.

summary.en: Write one aim and one testable hypothesis, and ask what you would do with each possible result.
summary.ur: Ek aim aur ek aazmaye ja sakne wali hypothesis likhein, aur poochhein har mumkina nateeje ke saath aap kya karenge.

summary.en: Start small, check ethics early and choose a gap rather than a repeat.
summary.ur: Chhote se shuru karein, ethics jaldi dekhein aur dohrane ke bajaye kami chunein.

front.ur: Aazmaye ja sakne wali hypothesis kya hai?

back.en: A specific, measurable prediction that data could show to be wrong.
back.ur: Khaas, naapne ke qabil peshgoi jise data ghalat sabit kar sake.

front.en: Why start with a small question?

back.en: You can complete it well, publish it and build on it.
back.ur: Aap isay achhi tarah mukammal, shaya aur is par construct kar sakte hain.

back.en: Asking what you would do differently with each possible result.
back.ur: Poochhna ke har mumkina nateeje ke saath aap kya mukhtalif karenge.

note.en: Matching the question to a design.
